item.title: Health Committee chairman warns MAM directives could delay medical testing in health centres
item.description: Franco Mercieca, chairman of Parliaments Health Committee, said Medical Association of Malta directives could hinder the introduction of point-of-care testing in Maltas health centres, and that patient safety must come first. His comments followed a committee meeting with MAM, primary health care officials and Mater Dei emergency department staff about point-of-care testing, which returns results within minutes and is particularly valuable in time-critical cases such as heart attacks and thrombosis. He also raised an inquiry into the procurement of the technology.

item.title: Isabelle Farrugia appointed first female chief executive of UHM Voice of the Workers
item.description: Isabelle Farrugia was appointed the first female chief executive of UHM Voice of the Workers at the unions 34th National Congress, making her the first woman to head a general trade union in Malta as the organisation marks 60 years. Kenneth Abela was appointed Director General and Josef Vella became Chairperson after 15 years leading the union. In her first address Farrugia highlighted traffic congestion, population growth, construction and energy as the countrys main challenges, and called for a long-term national plan agreed by both main parties under the patronage of the President.

item.title: Archbishop Scicluna urges Malta to reject economic apartheid against third-country nationals
item.description: Archbishop Charles Scicluna told the annual Diocesan Assembly that the Church in Malta must never be complicit in an "economic apartheid" separating Maltese citizens from the migrants who live and work in the country. The archbishop said a number of the Churchs charitable services could not function without the work of third-country nationals, and insisted that "we have a duty to treat them as human beings". More than 200 people from parishes, schools and other Church entities attended the Saturday assembly, which focused on the Churchs mission and work.

item.title: Financial Times feature revisits the acquittal of Yorgen Fenech over Daphne Caruana Galizias murder
item.description: Journalist Paul Caruana Galizia has published a new investigative feature in the Financial Times Weekend Magazine examining the September 2026 acquittal of Yorgen Fenech in the murder of his mother, Daphne Caruana Galizia. He wrote that the verdict "horrified my family and shocked the country" and that the family then "looked closer" at the case. He said Fenech did not respond to his questions, and that the accuseds three lawyers declined to answer and raised a conflict-of-interest complaint with the FT editor. The case, which has drawn national and international attention since 2017, remains without a conviction.

item.title: PN demands Finance Minister Caruana publish 2018 population report immediately
item.description: The Nationalist Party has called on Finance Minister Clyde Caruana to publish his 2018 report on population growth straight away, saying the public should not have to wait while he explains its contents. The report was commissioned by former prime minister Joseph Muscat in 2017 and dealt with the pressure rapid population growth would place on Malta's housing, hospitals, schools and infrastructure. Caruana said on Friday that he had written permission to release it and would hold a press conference after an overseas trip next week, but the PN said taxpayers paid up to €90,000 for the nearly 300-page document and that Caruana was paid between €80,000 and €90,000 to prepare it in a personal capacity while serving as Jobsplus CEO. Prime Minister Robert Abela has said he has no copy of the document.

item.title: Central Bank governor warns Malta cannot keep relying on cheap credit and subsidies
item.description: Central Bank governor Alexander Demarco told the Institute of Financial Services Malta that Malta must reduce its reliance on cheap credit, blanket energy subsidies and an ever-expanding workforce if it is to sustain growth, calling for a shift from policies that stimulate demand to a productivity-driven economy. He cautioned against relaxing mortgage lending restrictions, recalled the excess borrowing that triggered the 2008 financial crisis, and argued that subsidies must be timely, targeted and temporary rather than permanent. Demarco also urged restraint in government spending and public sector recruitment, while noting Malta starts from a position of strength with average growth of 5.3 per cent over the past four years and sound banks. His remarks come a month after the government made demand-side measures such as blanket energy subsidies and the annual superbonus a lynchpin of Budget 2027.

item.title: Labour MP calls for consensual sex between close-in-age minors to be decriminalised
item.description: Labour MP Ramona Attard asked parliament to discuss decriminalising consensual sexual activity between minors who are close in age, saying teenagers should not have their criminal records tarnished. The age of sexual consent in Malta is 16 and Article 204C of the Criminal Code carries a five-to-ten year sentence for sexual activity with someone under 16. While children under 14 are exempt from criminal responsibility and 14 and 15-year-olds can be held liable only if deemed sufficiently mature, with reduced penalties available where the activity is consensual and no abuse occurred, Attard argued these mitigations do not go far enough and that decriminalisation within clearly defined parameters should be considered.

item.title: Mental health decisions must be shaped by lived experiences, says Deputy PM Ian Borg
item.description: Speaking at the annual National Mental Health Services conference, Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg said mental health policy and services must be built around the real-life experiences of patients and their families. He reaffirmed the shift away from an institution-based model towards community-centred care, citing a planned regional hub in Bormla, a new acute mental health unit under construction at Mater Dei Hospital and the long-term vision for Mount Carmel Hospital. He stressed that acute care, Mount Carmel and community services must work together so patients and families have clear support after discharge.

item.title: Education ministry denies claims crucifixes are being removed from schools
item.description: The education ministry denied that any order was issued to remove crucifixes from Maltese schools, following the circulation of social media posts about the matter in recent days. The ministry said the allegations were completely false, that all crucifixes remain hanging on school walls and that children sing the Maltese national anthem every day. It described the presence of crucifixes and the anthem as integral parts of Maltese identity and culture and invited anyone with doubts to visit classrooms to check for themselves.

item.title: Man with two unlicensed firearms, one with a silencer, remanded in custody after Siġġiewi raid
item.description: A 45-year-old Italian man was remanded in custody after police found two loaded firearms, one fitted with a silencer, during a search of a property in Siġġiewi. Salvatore Rinaudo, born in Catania, Sicily, was arraigned before Magistrate Monica Vella on Friday and charged with possessing firearms or ammunition without a licence. The arrest followed a surveillance operation on a vehicle that had arrived from Sicily by catamaran and was followed to the Siġġiewi property; the two occupants were arrested in Kirkop. His defence challenged the legality of the arrest.

item.title: Protesters form human chain at Castille against Budget 2027 measures on third-country nationals
item.description: About 75 people formed a human chain on the steps beside Parliament on Friday evening and walked up to Castille, where a letter was read out and delivered to the prime minister and finance minister. Organised by TCN Alliance, Solidarjetà, Moviment Graffitti and TCNs United as part of the Green Ribbon Project campaign, the demonstrators called on government to withdraw the Budget 2027 measures affecting third-country nationals without long-term residency. TCN Alliance representative Patricia Graham said the measures were unfair and discriminatory, pointing to the rise in work permit application fees from €600 to €800, a new €400 annual charge on permit applications and renewals, a €33 monthly public transport charge and a monthly private car charge of about €83. The organisers also questioned the withdrawal of free childcare and public transport for TCNs resident in Malta for under five years, saying charging residents differently on the basis of nationality raises questions over constitutional and EU non-discrimination principles, and asked for proper consultation before the changes take effect next year.

item.title: Isabelle Farrugia elected first woman CEO of UĦM, Josef Vella becomes chairperson
item.description: Isabelle Farrugia was elected CEO of UĦM – Voice of the Workers at the union's 43rd national congress, the first woman to hold the post in its 60-year history. Farrugia rejected feminism, gender quotas and positive discrimination, telling delegates that women do not need special treatment to reach positions of power, and said her election proved the point. Outgoing CEO Josef Vella moved to a newly created non-executive chairperson role covering governance and financial accountability, while Kenneth Abela was elected director general. Farrugia urged government and opposition to agree on a long-term national plan covering traffic, population growth, construction and energy rather than five-year political cycles, and reaffirmed the union's political independence, with industrial action as a last resort.

item.title: Malta risks part of final €61.7m EU recovery payment over tribunal reform milestone
item.description: The European Commission said Malta had satisfactorily completed 26 of the 27 milestones in its final €61.7 million Recovery and Resilience Facility payment request but had not met a milestone on the independence of specialised tribunals. Malta has two months to respond before a final assessment, and the payment would be reduced by an amount corresponding to the outstanding reform if the Commission maintains its view. The request, submitted on 30 September, covers the new Blood, Tissue and Cell Centre, electricity distribution network investment, digitalisation grants for SMEs and access to finance under InvestEU.

item.title: SDM takes all eight Junior College council seats for first time in ten years
item.description: Studenti Demokristjani Maltin won all eight seats on the Junior College student council, taking 1,403 votes against 305 for Pulse, which had dominated the college's student politics for over a decade. Nationalist Party leader Alex Borg said the result showed young people wanted change, while MŻPN president Thomas De Martino congratulated SDM on returning to the helm after ten years. The eight elected members are Jake Borg (president), Jacob Spiteri (vice president), Elena Callus (general secretary), Shayen Mamo (social policy), Adam Abdilla (public relations), Jake Fasanelli (financial officer), Eric Zahra (culture and entertainment) and Melissa Sansone (education).

item.title: Planning Authority seals off illegal car wash at St Paul's Bay fuel station
item.description: The Planning Authority sealed off an illegal car wash at Dad's Fuel Station on Triq il-Mosta, St Paul's Bay, following years of resident complaints about noise from three power wash bays operated without a permit since 2017. The action was linked to an enforcement notice covering unauthorised works, including covered car wash bays, and criminal proceedings are understood to have been initiated after a noise complaint. The authority also sealed off an unauthorised road opening and illegal structures on Triq Pwales, saying development or change of use without planning permission can result in direct enforcement action.

item.title: Woman charged with grievously injuring man in Marsa scissors attack
item.description: A 42-year-old woman was charged on Friday with grievously injuring a man allegedly stabbed in the chest with a pair of scissors during an altercation in Triq il-Marsa in the early hours of Thursday. Police were called at around 2am after the pair, who had been drinking in a public garden, fell out. The accused, who claimed she acted in self-defence, denied the charge before magistrate Monica Vella and was remanded in custody. Inspector James Zammit and Attorney General lawyer Krista Spiteri Lucas prosecuted.

item.title: Animal welfare officers to be equipped with body cameras
item.description: Parliamentary Secretary for Animal Welfare Alicia Bugeja Said said the process of equipping Animal Welfare Directorate officers with body-worn cameras has begun, enabling them to record footage during inspections and investigations. Director Dennis Sciberras said further training and equipment would strengthen interventions in cruelty and neglect cases, and the government is considering allowing voluntary organisations to help gather evidence where circumstances permit. Work is ongoing with MCAST to bring the Ta' Qali animal hospital into operation, and discussions have begun on a dedicated animal welfare fund, with a record €3 million allocated to the sector in the 2027 Budget.

item.title: Food safety authority warns of wrong expiry date on egg packs
item.description: The Food Safety and Security Authority said packs of 30 Class A fresh eggs from Ave Maria Farm, weighing between 53 and 63 grams, were labelled with a best-before date of 26 December 2026 instead of the correct 26 November 2026. Consumers are advised not to eat the eggs beyond the correct best-before date. The authority stressed the eggs remain safe to eat until 26 November and that their quality and safety were not compromised by the labelling error. The affected product bears the egg packing centre code EPC 002.

item.title: Cycling NGO warns new national strategy lacks deadlines, targets and budget
item.description: Cycling advocacy group Rota welcomed the National Cycling Strategy 2026–2036 launched by the Ministry for Sustainable Mobility but warned that the absence of implementation deadlines, measurable targets and a dedicated budget risks undermining it, noting the 2018 strategy included timelines. Rota called on the ministry to publish a detailed implementation timetable, allocate a budget, set measurable targets and issue annual progress reports. The strategy proposes a national cycling route network, speed limits on designated routes, workplace facilities and cycling training for children and adults.

item.title: Study finds children turn to family and trusted adults for mental health support
item.description: Findings from the Family Ministry's EmpowerME project, run with the health and education ministries and University College Cork, were presented on World Children's Day. The study covered 1,135 pupils aged seven to 13 in five schools and found that children have a holistic understanding of mental health, believing family and those closest to them should be the first to help them, while they understand the concept mainly through everyday experience rather than clinical definitions. The project produced the first Mental Health Toolkit for children, parents and educators plus a digital toolkit under the Empowering Children App.

item.title: Man remanded over 314 messages to ex-girlfriend sent despite protection order
item.description: A 27-year-old man from Qormi was remanded in custody on Friday after pleading not guilty to harassing, threatening and insulting his former girlfriend and breaching a protection order issued in August 2026. The court heard that the woman, who reported the case to the police's Domestic Violence Unit on 18 November, received 314 messages and a number of calls between September and November, some allegedly containing threatening language. He was arrested on Thursday and charged with four offences, and the prosecution objected to bail because the victim had yet to testify, while the defence argued the messages were not one-sided.

item.title: Mayors approve resolution setting priorities for strengthening local government
item.description: Mayors of Malta and Gozo attending the Local Councils' Association Annual Mayors' Conference in Gozo voted to approve a resolution establishing five priorities for strengthening local government. The measures call for the option of mayors to serve full-time with a remuneration package reflecting the scope of each locality, and for councils to have active participation in determining the financial allocations made by central government. The conference also discussed demographic change, the forthcoming waste collection and management tender and the Maltese delegation to the European Committee of the Regions.

item.title: Over half of Gozo businesses expect to raise prices as labour shortages hit record high
item.description: A record 81 per cent of businesses in Gozo expect their operating costs to rise over the next six months and 53 per cent anticipate raising consumer prices, according to the latest Gozo Business Sentiment survey published on Saturday. It is the first time since the survey began in 2023 that a majority expect price increases, with manufacturing and industry worst affected. Labour shortages have overtaken rising costs as the biggest worry, cited by 58 per cent of firms, while 40 per cent flagged cost pressures. The survey was carried out in September by the Gozo Regional Development Authority and the Gozo Business Chamber.

item.title: IMF official: Malta among the fastest-growing economies in the EU
item.description: IMF deputy managing director Kenji Okamura said Malta is among the fastest-growing economies in the European Union during a visit to Valletta, where he met Prime Minister Robert Abela, Finance Minister Clyde Caruana and Central Bank governor Alexander Demarco. He praised strong tourism, expanding professional services and a resilient labour market, welcomed Malta's exit from the EU excessive deficit procedure, and urged structural reforms addressing infrastructure, skills shortages, innovation and Malta Vision 2050. He also explored the tourism and advanced manufacturing sectors and welcomed efforts to make tourism more sustainable.

item.title: Duke of Edinburgh's Award marks 65 years in Malta with 70-tree planting initiative
item.description: Seventy trees were planted between Rabat and Attard to mark the 65th anniversary of the Duke of Edinburgh's International Award in Malta, the government said on Saturday. The event, organised by the DofE Malta Foundation, was attended by Inclusion and Volunteering Minister Julia Farrugia and MCVS chief executive Mauro Pace Parascandolo. The planting is part of a programme funded through the MCVS Community Support Scheme, with further initiatives including a national meeting for Award leaders and a youth camp at the Scouts' campsite in Għajn Tuffieħa.

item.title: NPSPD urges EU states to guarantee equal services for children with disabilities
item.description: The National Society for Persons with Disability called on EU member states to fully implement the European Guarantee for Children, on the occasion of Universal Children's Day. Joining forces with COFACE Families Europe, the NPSPD said children with disabilities and their families still face barriers accessing healthcare, early education, school activities, suitable accommodation and adequate nutrition. The coalition noted that close to one in four children in Europe is at risk of poverty or social exclusion.

item.description: A 31-year-old man from Żejtun was arrested after police intercepted a post parcel containing four kilos of suspected cannabis valued at about €96,000, in an operation police said involved a controlled delivery. The man was charged with drug importation and trafficking and is expected to be arraigned in court. The arrest was announced on Saturday morning, hours after the interception.

item.title: Animal welfare officers to get body cameras as Budget 2027 sets aside record 3 million
item.description: Malta is to equip Animal Welfare Directorate officers with body cameras to support inspections and interventions, Parliamentary Secretary for Animal Welfare Alicia Bugeja Said told voluntary sector organisations. The government is also considering legislative amendments on dog breeding and the conditions in which domestic animals are kept, and would allow animal welfare NGOs to help gather evidence in suspected cruelty cases. Budget 2027 includes a record 3 million allocation for the sector, discussions have started on a dedicated animal welfare fund with the ministry responsible for local councils, and work is ongoing on the long-awaited Ta Qali animal hospital.

item.title: 161 people found living illegally in Malta over the past four weeks
item.description: Home Affairs and Security Minister Glenn Bedingfield said 161 people were found residing illegally in Malta over the past four weeks and are to be deported, with another 54 individuals already returned to their countries of origin or other EU member states. Operations were carried out in Birżebbuġa, Gudja, Kirkop, Żebbuġ, Marsa, Marsaxlokk, Mosta, San Ġwann, St Julian's, St Paul's Bay, Valletta, Sliema, Marsaskala and Żebbuġ in Gozo. The minister thanked Immigration Police and Detention Services officers for their work.

item.title: Home Affairs Minister calls fire safety a shared responsibility
item.description: Minister for Home Affairs and Security Glenn Bedingfield told a conference organised by the Insurance Association Malta that fire safety must go beyond emergency response, with more weight on prevention, planning and risk management. He said fire does not distinguish between insured and uninsured property, and that the cost of prevention should be weighed against the far greater human and financial consequences of an incident. He also praised the Civil Protection Department's work in preparedness, training and public awareness.

item.title: Culture minister Agius Galea vows to 'rise to the challenge' amid artist backlash
item.description: Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea said he would "rise to the challenge" of regaining the trust of the arts community after his remarks at the Festival of Ideas, including that artists think they are "God's gift to the world" and that his first four months in office were "traumatic". The artists' lobby has called for his resignation. Asked how he intended to rebuild trust, the minister said he was reaching out and was on his way to visit an artist, adding that "if you give up, you are not fit to be a minister".
